indieProjects.name: Poker AI: HomeStack
indieProjects.description: A league manager and live-game tracker for home poker nights. Friends join a league by invite code, the app runs the bank during the game, and an AI summary plus stats, awards and head-to-head records settle every argument afterwards. Solo-built with Expo and shipped to the App Store and Google Play, in English, Hebrew (RTL) and Spanish.

features.title: The bank does the math
features.description: Track buy-ins, re-buys and cash-outs live during the game, with one active game per league and settlements calculated automatically.

features.title: AI league summary
features.description: An LLM turns league history into a plain-language recap, returned as schema-validated structured output.

features.title: League & personal stats
features.description: ROI, win streaks, monthly profit leaders and season-by-season rankings for every player.

features.title: Head to head
features.description: Pick any two players and compare their record across the games they played together.

features.title: Awards & badges
features.description: MVP, Shark, Hot Streak and Comeback King are handed out automatically every month.

features.title: Invite links & RTL
features.description: Join a league from a universal link or code. Fully localized in English, Hebrew (right-to-left) and Spanish.

architecture: Type-Safe Generic Middleware: Uses TypeScript generics `<T extends Response>` to create a reusable higher-order function that preserves return type safety while adding authentication logic to any API handler

Multi-Platform Token Strategy: Seamlessly handles both native mobile (Bearer token via Authorization header) and web (HTTP-only cookies) authentication in a single codebase without platform-specific code duplication

Granular Error Handling: Distinguishes between JWT expiration, invalid tokens, and verification errors using typed error classes from the `jose` library, enabling precise client-side error recovery strategies

Security Best Practices: Implements proper JWT verification with secret keys, extracts user context from validated tokens, and follows the principle of "fail closed" by defaulting to 401 Unauthorized on any authentication failure
performance: Server state lives in TanStack Query, with FlashList for long player and game lists
React Compiler and Reanimated keep interactions on the UI thread at 60fps
Custom hooks with AbortController cancel in-flight requests on unmount
Player and game photos are stored on Cloudflare R2 instead of the database
deployment: EAS Build for cloud iOS and Android builds, EAS Update for over-the-air fixes
API routes deployed with EAS Hosting next to the app, backed by Neon serverless Postgres
GitHub Actions runs lint and 1,390+ Jest tests with coverage on every push
Husky pre-push hook runs the full suite before anything reaches the remote
tradeoffs: Chose Expo managed workflow for faster development over bare React Native for maximum control
Used Expo API routes instead of a separate backend to keep one codebase and ship faster
Called the LLM over a plain HTTP client with zod validation instead of adopting a full AI framework
Kept typed JWT auth in-house (jose) rather than adding a hosted auth provider
challenges: Handling edge cases in game history parsing and validation
Optimizing chart rendering performance with large datasets
Managing app state across offline/online transitions
Balancing feature richness with app size constraints for mobile
learnings: Importance of designing for offline-first from day one
Value of comprehensive error boundaries and crash reporting (Sentry)
Mobile users expect instant feedback - optimistic updates are critical
App Store review process requires patience and attention to guidelines

indieProjects.name: Mibo: Chores Tracker
indieProjects.description: A kids chores and allowance app where the child is the primary user. Parents set chores and rewards; each child ticks off their own list on their own device — offline if needed — earns coins instantly and raises a pet that cheers them on. Released on the App Store for iPhone and iPad in November 2026.

features.title: Instant rewards
features.description: Children earn coins the moment a chore is done, on their own phone or tablet — even offline.

features.title: Photo approval
features.description: Parents see the photo and tap approve, or reject it so the chore comes back as a redo.

features.title: A pet that cheers them on
features.description: Built-in motivation: a companion that grows as chores get done.

features.title: Rewards & real allowance
features.description: Parents choose what coins buy and convert them into real allowance at their own rate.

architecture: pnpm + Turborepo monorepo: Expo app, Hono API and a shared package for types and validation
Children never have an email or password — only parents authenticate, through Clerk
Household is the unit of the product: timezone, currency, entitlement, parents and children
performance: Chores complete on the child's device first and sync later, so it works offline
deployment: API on Railway, mobile builds through EAS, subscriptions through RevenueCat
tradeoffs: One evening summary for parents instead of a notification per chore

indieProjects.name: Drivers Task Manager
indieProjects.tagline: Real-time task coordination for Toyota dealership operations
indieProjects.description: Full-stack Progressive Web App that replaced manual Excel workflows with a real-time task system for a Toyota dealership. Drivers, desk staff and managers coordinate vehicle logistics with instant status updates, push notifications, and signature and photo capture — in a Hebrew right-to-left interface that keeps working offline.

features.title: Real-Time Sync
features.description: Instant status updates across all users - drivers, desk staff, and managers see changes immediately

features.title: KPI Charts
features.description: Per-driver completion and duration charts, status breakdowns and weekly trends for managers

features.title: Admin Dashboard
features.description: Tasks, drivers, vehicles, an audit log and role-based access for admins, managers, drivers and viewers

features.title: Kanban & Calendar
features.description: Visual task board with drag-and-drop plus a calendar view, with late-task checks and push notifications

architecture: Designed as a Progressive Web App for cross-platform compatibility without app store deployment
Real-time data synchronization using Supabase Realtime subscriptions
Role-based access control for drivers, desk staff, and managers
Offline-first for field use: IndexedDB queues and a service worker with background sync
performance: Optimistic UI updates for instant feedback on task status changes
Efficient real-time subscriptions to minimize bandwidth usage
Lazy loading of dashboard analytics to prioritize core task management
deployment: Deployed on Vercel with automatic preview deployments for testing
Environment-based configuration for staging and production
Automated database migrations with Supabase CLI
tradeoffs: Chose PWA over native app to enable rapid deployment without app store review process
Used Supabase for faster development over custom backend infrastructure
Prioritized real-time sync over offline editing to match dealership workflow needs
challenges: Designing intuitive mobile UI for quick task updates while driving
Managing real-time state across multiple concurrent users
Balancing push notification frequency to be helpful without being intrusive
learnings: PWAs can effectively replace native apps for business tools
Real-time features dramatically improve team coordination
Close collaboration with end users is essential for workflow tools
